articles.heading: General Provisions for Arbiter Titles
articles.content: FIDE awards two arbiter titles: FIDE Arbiter (FA) and International Arbiter (IA). Both titles are awarded for life unless revoked. Candidates must demonstrate knowledge of the Laws of Chess, FIDE regulations, and practical arbiting experience. Titles are awarded by FIDE upon application through the national federation.

articles.heading: Arbiter Norms
articles.content: An arbiter norm is a performance credit awarded for serving as an arbiter at a qualifying event. Norms are graded A, B, C, or D depending on the level of the event. An Olympiad, World Championship, or Continental Championship yields an A-norm. Norms accumulate over a career and contribute to title eligibility. The exact norm requirements are updated periodically by the FIDE Arbiters' Commission.

articles.heading: Requirements for the Title of FIDE Arbiter
articles.content: To be awarded the FIDE Arbiter title, a candidate must: pass a FIDE Arbiter seminar exam with a score of at least 80%, serve as arbiter at a minimum number of qualifying events, demonstrate knowledge of the Laws of Chess and tournament regulations, and have the application endorsed by their national federation. The candidate must also hold a FIDE ID.

articles.heading: Requirements for the Title of International Arbiter
articles.content: To be awarded the International Arbiter title, a candidate must already hold the FIDE Arbiter title, accumulate a required number of arbiter norms at international events, serve as Chief Arbiter or Deputy Chief Arbiter at qualifying events, and demonstrate proficiency in a FIDE official language. The IA title requires higher-level events than the FA title.

articles.heading: Training of Chess Arbiters
articles.content: FIDE Arbiter seminars are organised by FIDE, continental federations, and national federations. Seminars must follow the FIDE-approved curriculum and be conducted by FIDE-accredited lecturers. The seminar includes theoretical instruction and a written examination. Passing the exam is mandatory for the FA title application. Seminars are listed on the FIDE website in advance.

articles.heading: Classification of Arbiters
articles.content: Active FAs and IAs are classified into Categories A, B, C, and D based on their level of activity and the events they have officiated. Category A is the highest, requiring experience at top-level events. An arbiter must serve at a minimum number of events per year to remain active. Inactive arbiters retain their title but lose their classification category.

articles.heading: Appointment of Arbiters in World Events
articles.content: Arbiters for FIDE World Events are selected by panels maintained by the FIDE Arbiters' Commission. Appointment to World Championships and Olympiads requires Category A or equivalent status. Arbiters must not have a conflict of interest with any participant. The Chief Arbiter for a World event is approved by the FIDE Presidential Board.

articles.heading: Arbiter Disciplinary Regulations — Offences
articles.content: An arbiter may be subject to disciplinary action for: serious errors in applying the Laws of Chess, misconduct or behaviour unbecoming of an arbiter, failure to follow FIDE regulations, corruption or manipulation of results, and failure to submit required reports. Complaints must be submitted to the ARB Disciplinary Sub-Committee with supporting evidence.

articles.heading: Arbiter Disciplinary — Sanctions
articles.content: Sanctions available to the ARB Disciplinary Sub-Committee include: warning, suspension from arbiting for a specified period, downgrading of classification category, suspension of the arbiter title, and revocation of the arbiter title. All sanctions are subject to appeal. Serious offences may be referred to the FIDE Ethics Commission.
